## Evidence and limits
- [ ] Inspect available original sources before asking the author to repeat information.
- [ ] Record what each source supports and does not support, including date and context.
- [ ] Preserve contrary evidence and distinguish duplicate/copy-forward sources.
- [ ] Identify missing evidence, competent reviewer and the next bounded action.
- [ ] Split compound claims; do not turn questions into findings.
- [ ] Link corrections and affected passages without overwriting originals.

## Disposition
Unreviewed / source-attested / independently supported within stated scope / disputed / unsupported / contradicted / superseded / not empirical.

Remaining limits and dependent issues:

Publication of an approved working source is separate from factual clearance. First-person experience does not need external certification to be preserved. Do not infer motive, guilt, clinical causation or lack of action from the mere absence of a record in the working set.
